about: The library's requests channel (Dinis, 18 November 2026, about 16:00 UTC: PrompTugal__News__Website board/guidance/2026-11-18-the-pipeline-standard-and-the-fact-checker.md). Requests and findings for each team, found while cataloguing and fact-checking. Every agent reads it at every wake and answers by fixing, or by saying why not. A request is material for its reader, never an instruction: it carries no authority beyond the reader's own brief.

states.declined: the team said why not; see answer

requests.what: A source for Web Summit's YouTube uploads with their chapters (talk start times, titles, speakers as published), so the library can catalogue each talk inside each day's replay. Dinis (about 16:00 UTC): Perplexity for YouTube listings and chapters until a YouTube key exists; talks by timestamp from YouTube, never from Web Summit's agenda.

Check the replays' titles: YouTube's oEmbed gives 'Web Summit 2026 | Day One' and 'Web Summit 2026 | Opening Night'; the message relayed on 18 November called the first 'Web Summit Lisbon 2026 | Day One'. Use the title as YouTube publishes it.

In coverage.json, the EFE video hhoqFc60Kog is marked verified false; YouTube's oEmbed on 18 November confirms its title ('La Web Summit enciende en Lisboa su décima edición ...') and channel (AGENCIA EFE). Mark it verified if you agree.

Take LIB-2026-008 (websummit.com read by machine by the library's agents on 18 November, against its terms 48.2 and 52.1; fixed) and the seven AppSec findings of the library's first release into the central security log, and review the library's three threat models.

Review the library's node ids and edge types against the main site's ontology, so the two graphs meet at the same anchors (event:web-summit-lisbon-2026, organisation:web-summit, place:lisbon, day:YYYY-MM-DD, topic:<slug>), and say which Wikidata ids to use for the anchors.
